vocabulary.meaning_en: great comfort and expensive things
vocabulary.example: They stayed in a luxury hotel.

vocabulary.meaning_en: very comfortable and expensive
vocabulary.example: The car has luxurious leather seats.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the name of a company's products
vocabulary.example: This is a famous sports brand.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who designs things; made by a famous designer
vocabulary.note_ar: من design = يصمم؛ designer clothes = ملابس الماركات العالمية
vocabulary.example: She only wears designer clothes.
vocabulary.note_en: From "design"; designer clothes = clothes from famous brands.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small shop that sells special, expensive things
vocabulary.example: She bought her dress from a small boutique.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a product made in small numbers only
vocabulary.example: This watch is a limited edition; only 500 were made.
vocabulary.note_en: limit = a maximum amount; edition = one version or release of a product.

vocabulary.meaning_en: only for certain people or in one place
vocabulary.example: Members get exclusive offers.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small piece of paper or cloth with information on a product
vocabulary.example: Read the label before you wash it.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a symbol that represents a company
vocabulary.example: The shirt has a small logo on the front.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a new popular style or direction
vocabulary.example: Wide trousers are the latest trend.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having good personal style
vocabulary.example: He always looks stylish, even in jeans.

vocabulary.meaning_en: following the latest fashion
vocabulary.example: Short jackets are fashionable this year.

vocabulary.meaning_en: graceful, classic and refined
vocabulary.example: She looked elegant in her evening gown.

vocabulary.meaning_en: very good in quality
vocabulary.example: They only use high-quality cotton.

vocabulary.meaning_en: animal skin used for bags and shoes
vocabulary.example: This leather bag will last for years.

vocabulary.meaning_en: rings, necklaces, bracelets, etc.
vocabulary.note_ar: jewelry بحرف l واحد في أمريكا، jewellery بحرفين في بريطانيا؛ لا تُعدّ وتعامل كمفرد
vocabulary.example: Her jewellery is very expensive.
vocabulary.note_en: "Jewelry" (one l) is American; "jewellery" (two l's) is British. It is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

vocabulary.meaning_en: jewellery worn around the wrist
vocabulary.example: He gave her a golden bracelet.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a liquid with a nice smell that you put on your skin
vocabulary.example: What perfume are you wearing?

vocabulary.meaning_en: products like make-up and creams
vocabulary.note_ar: المفرد cosmetic يُستخدم غالباً كصفة: cosmetic surgery = جراحة تجميلية
vocabulary.example: She works in a cosmetics shop.
vocabulary.note_en: The singular "cosmetic" is mostly used as an adjective: cosmetic surgery = surgery to improve how you look.

vocabulary.meaning_en: extra things you wear with clothes: watch, belt, glasses
vocabulary.example: A good watch is my favourite accessory.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a jacket and trousers made from the same cloth
vocabulary.example: He wore a dark suit to the wedding.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a long formal dress for special events
vocabulary.example: She wore a red evening gown to the party.
vocabulary.note_en: Longer and more formal than a normal dress.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the long stage where models walk in a fashion show
vocabulary.note_ar: runway أمريكي (من مدرج الطائرات)، catwalk بريطاني (من مشية القطة)
vocabulary.example: The models walked down the runway.
vocabulary.note_en: "Runway" is American (like an airport runway); "catwalk" is British (from the way a cat walks).

vocabulary.meaning_en: a special box for a present
vocabulary.example: The perfume came in a beautiful gift box.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to move by putting one foot forward
vocabulary.example: He stepped inside the room.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a collection of gold, jewels or valuable things
vocabulary.example: The pirates hid their treasure on an island.

vocabulary.meaning_en: shining with small points of light
vocabulary.example: She wore a sparkling necklace.
vocabulary.note_en: From "sparkle" (to shine with small flashes of light).

vocabulary.meaning_en: known all over the world
vocabulary.example: Paris has many world-famous museums.
vocabulary.note_en: A compound adjective (two words working as one adjective).

vocabulary.meaning_en: to stop for a moment because you are not sure
vocabulary.example: She hesitated before answering.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having a certain value
vocabulary.example: This old coin is worth a lot of money.
vocabulary.note_en: worth a fortune = worth a lot of money.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a very large amount of money
vocabulary.example: That house must have cost a fortune.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to put liquid on something in small drops
vocabulary.example: She sprayed some perfume on her neck.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the joint between your hand and arm
vocabulary.example: He wears his watch on his left wrist.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to strongly try to make someone do something
vocabulary.example: My friend urged me to apply for the job.
vocabulary.note_en: Pattern: urge someone to do something.

vocabulary.meaning_en: unable to escape from a place or situation
vocabulary.example: He felt trapped in his boring job.
vocabulary.note_en: trap = something used to catch an animal or a person.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to trick someone
vocabulary.example: Don't let them fool you with low prices.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not certain
vocabulary.note_ar: = not sure، لكنها صفة يمكن وضعها قبل الاسم: an unsure smile
vocabulary.example: She gave him an unsure smile.
vocabulary.note_en: Means "not sure", but it can go before a noun: an unsure smile.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a written promise to repair a product if it breaks
vocabulary.example: The TV comes with a two-year warranty.

fine_lines.title: fashionable vs stylish vs elegant
fine_lines.explanation_ar: fashionable شخص يلبس ما هو رائج الآن ويتبع الموضة الحالية. stylish شخص له ذوق وستايل خاص ويعرف كيف ينسّق ملابسه، حتى لو لم يتبع الموضة. elegant درجة أعلى: رقي وفخامة مع بساطة، وعادة مرتبطة باللبس الكلاسيكي مثل البدلات الرسمية وفساتين السهرة.

examples.sentence: The singer always wears the most fashionable clothes.
My friend looks stylish in a simple shirt and jeans.
The princess looked elegant in a long white gown.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A fashionable person wears what is popular right now and follows the latest trends. A stylish person has their own good taste and knows how to match clothes, even without following trends. Elegant is a step higher: graceful and classy but simple, usually linked to classic clothes like formal suits and evening gowns.

fine_lines.title: at a bargain price vs for a bargain price
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المعنى واحد (بسعر لُقطة) لكن الاستخدام مختلف. at نستخدمها عند عرض شيء للبيع (أبيعه لك عند هذا السعر). for نستخدمها عندما نتكلم عن شيء اشتريناه مقابل سعر معين.

examples.sentence: I can sell you this watch at a bargain price.
I bought this jacket for a bargain price.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Same meaning (at a very low price), but used differently. "At" is used when offering something for sale (I'll sell it to you at this price). "For" is used when talking about something you bought for a certain price.

fine_lines.title: runway vs catwalk
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنتان منصة عرض الأزياء. runway (أمريكي) اشتقاق وظيفي من مدرج الطائرات لأنه طريق مستقيم يُمشى عليه. catwalk (بريطاني) اشتقاق تصويري: العارضات يمشين بوضع قدم أمام الأخرى مثل القطة.

examples.sentence: The dress came straight from the runway.
She walked the catwalk in London.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean the long stage in a fashion show. "Runway" (American) comes from an airport runway, a straight path to walk on. "Catwalk" (British) is a picture word: models walk with one foot in front of the other, like a cat.

fine_lines.title: a few vs a little
fine_lines.explanation_ar: a few مع الأشياء المعدودة (items, bracelets)، و a little مع الأشياء غير المعدودة (jewellery, money, water). لذلك نقول only a few items exist لأن items تُعد.

examples.sentence: She only wears a little jewellery.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "A few" goes with countable things (items, bracelets); "a little" goes with uncountable things (jewellery, money, water). So we say "only a few items exist" because items can be counted.

fine_lines.title: unsure vs not sure
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المعنى واحد (غير متأكد). لكن unsure صفة يمكن استخدامها وحدها أو قبل الاسم (an unsure smile)، أما not sure فلا يمكن وضعها قبل الاسم.

examples.sentence: She gave him an unsure smile.
Ali was not sure about the box.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Same meaning (not certain). But "unsure" is an adjective that can stand alone or go before a noun (an unsure smile), while "not sure" cannot go before a noun.

expressions.example: The suit was cheap, and they gave me a tie into the bargain.
That painting is worth a fortune.

expressions.meaning_ar: قلبه يدق بسرعة (من الخوف أو الحماس)
expressions.example: She opened the letter, her heart racing.
expressions.meaning_en: heart beating fast (from fear or excitement)

expressions.example: We are selling these phones at a bargain price.
expressions.meaning_en: at a very low price (when selling)

expressions.example: Book the flat now, before someone else does.

expressions.meaning_ar: ليس كذا بل كذا (نفي وإثبات للتشويق)
expressions.example: It was not gold but a luxury collection of jewellery.
expressions.meaning_en: not this, but that (used to surprise or correct)

expressions.example: They added a small bag of cosmetics for free.

grammar.title: Reported commands: told / asked / urged someone (not) to
grammar.explanation_ar: لنقل الأمر أو الطلب نقول: فعل الطلب + الشخص + to + الفعل الأساسي، تماماً مثل العربية «قال لي أن أفتح الباب». يمكن اختيار الفعل حسب طريقة الكلام: told (قال)، asked (طلب بلطف)، ordered (أمر)، urged (ألحّ). وللنفي نقول not to وليس to not.
examples: "Open the door." → He told me to open the door.
"Don't stop the car." → He asked me not to stop the car.
"Sit down." → The teacher ordered Ali to sit down.
grammar.explanation_en: To report a command or request, use: verb + person + to + base verb (He told me to open the door). Choose the verb that fits how it was said: told, asked (politely), ordered, urged (pushed strongly). For negatives, say "not to", not "to not".

grammar.title: Compound adjectives
grammar.explanation_ar: الصفة المركبة كلمتان أو أكثر تعملان معاً كصفة واحدة. الأفضل وضع شرطة بينهما، والأهم أن الصفات لا تُجمع في الإنجليزية، فنقول a five-star hotel وليس five-stars. أنماطها: رقم + اسم، اسم + صفة، صفة + اسم.
examples: a five-star hotel, a ten-minute break, a two-hour flight
world-famous brand, ice-cold water, sugar-free drink
grammar.explanation_en: A compound adjective is two or more words working together as one adjective. It's best to use a hyphen, and remember that adjectives are never plural in English, so we say "a five-star hotel", not "five-stars". Patterns: number + noun, noun + adjective, adjective + noun.

grammar.title: is / are being + past participle (passive, now)
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم am / is / are being + التصريف الثالث للتعبير عن شيء يحدث الآن بصيغة المبني للمجهول. وفي الماضي was / were being.
grammar.explanation_en: We use am / is / are being + past participle for a passive action happening now. In the past, use was / were being.

questions.question: Which is correct?
questions.explanation_en: Compound adjectives are never plural: five-star.

questions.question: "Don't open the door." → He told me ___ the door.
questions.explanation_ar: في نقل النهي نقول not to + الفعل.
questions.explanation_en: For a negative command in reported speech, use not to + verb.

questions.question: My friend kept insisting. He ___ me to apply for the job.
questions.explanation_ar: urge someone to = يلحّ على شخص أن يفعل شيئاً.
questions.explanation_en: urge someone to = push someone strongly to do something.

questions.question: A person who always wears what is trendy right now is:
The princess wore a classic long gown. She looked very ___.
questions.explanation_ar: elegant = راقٍ وفخم مع بساطة، مرتبط باللبس الكلاسيكي.
questions.explanation_en: Elegant = graceful and classy but simple, linked to classic clothes.

questions.question: The vendor said, "I'll sell it to you ___ a bargain price."
questions.explanation_ar: عند عرض الشيء للبيع نقول at a bargain price.
questions.explanation_en: When offering something for sale, we say "at a bargain price".

questions.question: "Into the bargain" means:
questions.explanation_ar: into the bargain = فوق البيعة / بالإضافة إلى ذلك.
questions.explanation_en: Into the bargain = as an extra; in addition.

questions.question: "Limited edition" means the product:
questions.explanation_en: Limited edition = only a small number were made.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
choices: She gave him a not sure smile.
She gave him an unsure smile.
She gave him a sure not smile.
She gave him an unsurely smile.
questions.explanation_ar: unsure صفة يمكن وضعها قبل الاسم، أما not sure فلا.
questions.explanation_en: "Unsure" can go before a noun, but "not sure" cannot.

questions.question: In British English, the runway in a fashion show is called the:
